semantics: Native Antigravity host profile (Plan 032 Phase 8, ADR 0030): the artifact vocabularies a native Antigravity package may use, pinned to the CLI release line of the docs changelog baseline (the docs lag the CLI: agy 1.2.14 is installed and agy changelog shows 1.2.15) and built on the guides plus the observations of plan 031. Antigravity is this repository's origin dialect, but the package is authored from the Semantic Core and these vocabularies, never from the legacy files. Surfaces (Antigravity 2.0, the CLI, the IDE) share the .agents/ workspace layout; the global directories differ.

layout.components: skills/<name>/SKILL.md, agents/<name>.md, rules/<name>.md, mcp_config.json, hooks.json, sidecars/<name>/sidecar.json

projectAgentsDiscovery.note: Workspace agents in .agents/agents/<name>.md and .agents/agents/<name>/agent.md are discovered, both layouts (plan 031, agy 1.2.14); the 1.2.11 release notes fix finding them in already-trusted workspaces, under --agent, in headless runs and in the /agents panel. Plain agy agents is empty even where --agent resolves; use --add-dir or the /agents panel to check discovery.

hooksInAgentFrontmatter.note: Any hooks: key in an agent file removes the agent from discovery, --agent and invoke_subagent (observed on agy 1.2.14, plan 031), and the legacy lane writes one into every agent. A native agent carries none; guards go in .agents/hooks.json.

hookFile.note: .agents/hooks.json, ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json and a plugin hooks.json hold command hooks on five events; a hook is workspace-wide with no documented per-agent scoping, but it fires for a subagent's calls as well as the main agent's (observed on agy 1.2.15). The guard ships as .agents/hooks.json plus .agents/hooks/agents-united-guard.js; the native install lane copies the script and merges the one key agents-united-guard into an existing hooks.json, never overwriting the user's hooks (ADR 0031 addendum). Observed on agy 1.2.16 (2026-10-03) through the files installed by the lane itself (agents add --native, not copied by hand): echo git push --force was denied with the guard's own message.

subagentInvocation.note: A main agent holding invoke_subagent reaches a workspace agent by name, including a mainAgent: false one; subagent: false refuses it ("not found or not allowed to be invoked"); a hooks: key makes it "not found" (plan 031, agy 1.2.14). On agy 1.2.15 a call with Prompt, Role, TypeName and Workspace reached the native code-reviewer, and the workspace copy won over a same-named agent in the global ~/.gemini/config/agents on the maintainer machine (observed once).

parallelSubagents.note: One invoke_subagent call with two specs created both subagents in the same second and both answered (observed, agy 1.2.15); the tasks were too short to show whether the runs overlap in time, so concurrent execution is documented but not proven.

hostEnforcedToolRestriction.note: Observed on agy 1.2.15 (2026-10-02, host-library/antigravity/observations): an agent whose tools: list held only view_file, list_dir and grep_search could not create a file and no file was created, while a control agent whose list added write_to_file created it, so the host withholds a tool outside the list and a read-only role is read-only by what it holds. A misspelled tool name can still hang the subagent (docs).

unifiedPermissionEngine.note: The permission presets (Default, Request Review, Turbo), command(...) rules and the default-on terminal sandbox exist on macOS and Linux; Windows keeps the earlier terminal-execution policy and a preview sandbox toggle, so any claim about sandboxed commands needs a non-Windows run. Observed on Linux (WSL Ubuntu, agy 1.2.15, headless) the permissions page did not hold for the CLI: a plain command was not run silently in a sandbox but needed permission (see cliDefaultPermission), and the CLI reference, which says the sandbox is off by default, matched.

workflows.note: Markdown workflows (/workflow-name, 12,000 characters each) are deprecated in favour of skills from November 1, 2026 (2026-11-01); the package authors none, and every skill is already a slash command.

builtinOrchestrators.note: /boost and /teamwork-preview are host features on paid plans with their own agents; a package neither installs nor configures them and its own orchestrator must not depend on them.

skillFrontmatterExtras.note: Only name and description are documented for a skill. Observed on agy 1.2.16 (2026-10-03, observations/2026-10-03-agy-1.2.16-probes.md): a real-folder copy of a registry skill with a multi-line description, a nested metadata: block and the Claude-only disable-slash-command: true was listed by the host exactly like a minimal name-and-description skill, so those keys do not stop a skill being listed. What metadata and disable-slash-command do on this host was not tried.

skillInstallMethod.note: Observed on agy 1.2.16 (Windows, headless, 2026-10-03, observations/2026-10-03-agy-1.2.16-probes.md): in one project, two skills held as real folders (a minimal one, and a registry skill copied in) were listed, a global skill was listed, and the 36 skills installed by the default agents add method, NTFS junctions into the registry (--symlink), were not listed (the count was the 58 global skills plus the 2 real folders). This is the cause of the absence recorded in observations/2026-10-03-agy-1.2.15-skills.md, not the frontmatter and not workspace trust. So the default install is not served on this host. Decision (maintainer, 2026-10-03, ADR 0033): with the native lane on, the skills in .agents/skills/ are installed as real copies whatever the method (an explicit --copy has the same effect; each file is recorded as a copy with its hash, an existing link install migrates on the next install or agents update, and an edited copy is not overwritten without --force); without the lane the install is unchanged, but the doctor and agents add warn that agy lists real folders and not links. Confirmed in one real session (observations/2026-10-03-agy-1.2.16-lane-skill-copies.md): the 36 skills of a --native install were listed, including the three project skills that were not listed as junctions. Not established: POSIX symlinks on Linux or macOS, file symlinks (a symlinked rule or agent), a junction that stays inside the workspace, the total the model reported, a Linux or macOS run of the copies, and any agy version other than 1.2.15 and 1.2.16.

geminiMd.note: Observed on agy 1.2.16 (Windows, headless, 2026-10-03): a marker line in a frontmatter-less .agents/rules/GEMINI.md and another in .agents/GEMINI.md were both visible to the agent, so GEMINI.md is read without frontmatter in both places, unlike the other files of .agents/rules/. With the native lane installed the agent also had the native always_on git-guardrails rule, and the same policy (never force-push) was visible once from each text, so the legacy GEMINI.md overlaps the native always_on rules rather than being replaced by them. Not established: the symlinked GEMINI.md that the default install creates (the probe used a real file), the size cost of the overlap, and whether the lane should omit the legacy file.

skillNames.note: The docs name rule is lowercase with hyphens, and every skill becomes a slash command. One registry skill was not clean: it kept an underscore in its .agents/skills copy (the Claude and Cline projections normalised it), so it was renamed generative-ui on 2026-10-03; that the renamed skill loads on this host is still not shown: a real headless session listed none of the project skills at all (observations/2026-10-03-agy-1.2.15-skills.md), and the cause was found afterwards (see skillInstallMethod: the skills were junctions, which the host does not list, so the rename was not the cause); a real-folder copy of generative-ui itself was not tried. One name is still shared with a built-in: grill-me and the built-in /grill-me, and which wins was not tried (tests/native-antigravity-skills.test.ts pins it as the only exception).

registryFiles.note: The agy changelog (1.2.10) describes agents.json, skills.json, rules.json and plugins.json registries whose directory entries load only the items directly inside the directory unless include_only names a nested one; the docs describe only .agents/rules.json, so treat the others as observed in release notes.

mcpWiring.note: The native lane merges the servers a bundle's agents declare by name into .agents/mcp_config.json (ADR 0032; the entries are registry/hosts/antigravity/mcp/servers.json, one per declared name, command and args only): the user's own servers, order, indent and line endings are kept, a key is ours only while the lockfile records it, and a name the user already has stays theirs. It never writes a secret: no env, headers or oauth block is shipped, and a server that needs a credential (github, firecrawl, stitch, figma) is not written at all (ADR 0032 addendum 2): the install prints its entry and the variable it needs, for the user to add once they hold the credential; an entry an older release wrote switched off is removed on the next install or agents update unless the user switched it on or edited it. Observed on agy 1.2.16 (Windows, headless, 2026-10-03, observations/2026-10-03-agy-1.2.16-probes.md): the workspace file is read in a session; a stdio server receives agy's own environment; a ${VAR} placeholder in env is not expanded (the server got the literal text), so none is written; a server whose command is not installed did not delay or break the run (10 s). Contradicting the docs and the switched-off design, a server marked disabled: true in the workspace file still started (one observation; agy's own global file stores disabled the same way and agy mcp list honours it there), so a credentialed server shipped switched off could be launched in every session, which is why none is written now. Unverified: why (the workspace loader, or headless mode), whether agy mcp enable|disable writes the same field, and whether an agent mcpServers: entry resolves (the native agents carry none).

surfaces.note: Antigravity 2.0, the CLI and the IDE share the .agents/ workspace layout and the hooks, rules and skills formats, but their global directories differ (~/.gemini/config, ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli) and everything here was observed on the CLI.

rulesFrontmatter.note: Every .md file inside .agents/rules/ must start with frontmatter declaring a valid trigger (always_on, model_decision, glob or manual), and the docs say a file without one is silently discarded. Observed on agy 1.2.15: with the legacy frontmatter-less rules the agent listed NONE of the persistent rules, and with the native rules it saw the two always_on ones (model_decision rules reach it as pointers). The 24 KB per-file and 20,000-token aggregate limits apply.

hookContract.note: Observed on agy 1.2.15 (observations, 2026-10-02): the hook command runs with the folder holding hooks.json (.agents/) as its working directory, so a relative script path is relative to it; the payload carries artifactDirectoryPath, conversationId, modelName, stepIdx, toolCall (name and args, CommandLine for run_command and TargetFile for the file writers), transcriptPath and workspacePaths. An answer with no decision ({}), non-JSON output and a non-zero exit each block the call ("tool call denied by pre-tool hook", empty reason for {}), so a guard must always answer. deny delivers its reason to the agent verbatim, a subagent's call is denied the same way and the denial text comes back through the parent, and ask falls back to the user's permission settings (a workspace write went through, a command stayed gated and was auto-denied headless). With the sandbox on (proceed-in-sandbox, Linux), a hook answering ask did not force a prompt: a normal command ran without one, so ask defers to the user's own permission settings there as well, and the guard needs no change.

cliDefaultPermission.note: Observed on Linux (WSL Ubuntu, agy 1.2.15): with default settings a plain echo was auto-denied in a headless run ("a tool required the command permission that headless mode cannot prompt for"), i.e. toolPermission request-review with no sandbox, as the CLI reference states and not as the permissions page describes for the Default preset; the --sandbox flag alone did not change that. Running commands in the sandbox without prompting needs toolPermission proceed-in-sandbox together with enableTerminalSandbox (or a command() allow rule) in settings.json; that was then tried, temporarily and with the maintainer's consent (see terminalSandboxLinux). The same default on Windows.

terminalSandboxLinux.note: Observed on Linux (WSL Ubuntu, agy 1.2.15, headless) with enableTerminalSandbox true and toolPermission proceed-in-sandbox set temporarily in the CLI settings.json (restored afterwards, checksum verified): a plain command ran without a prompt; the network was cut (curl: could not resolve host, exit 6); ~/.ssh looked empty inside the sandbox while it holds four files outside it, so the sandbox hides it; a write to the home directory failed with "Read-only file system" and no file was created. The guard hook's ask answer did not force a prompt: a normal command ran and a forced push was still denied. One build on one machine; macOS, Windows (older system) and the 2.0 and IDE surfaces were not tried.
